title: Functionally diverse stands promote leaf litter decomposition irrespective of litter species' resource acquisition strategy
content:
Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog.


Abstract

Stand functional diversity (RaoQ) and stand functional composition in terms of the functional traits of the component species (CWM trait) are critical for ecosystem processes and functioning, such as litter decomposition and associated nutrient cycling. Litter decomposition rates could differ among stands varying in functional diversity and composition because of interspecific variation of resource economic traits in litter quality as well as differences in microenvironmental conditions. However, whether and how functionally diverse stands with different microenvironmental conditions change the litter decomposition rates among functionally contrasting species is poorly understood. Here, we hypothesized that stand functional diversity would promote litter decomposition of resource acquisitive, intermediate and conservative species but with inconsistent strengths, because of the potential positive effects of higher probability for litter nutrient exchange or facilitative microclimate in diverse stands. Conservative species' litter might benefit less from the positive stand diversity effect than intermediate species' litter, and then acquisitive species' litter (Hypothesis 1). Meanwhile, we hypothesized two alternative scenarios for the effect of stand functional composition: First, acquisitive species' litter would decompose faster in stands dominated by acquisitive species, while conservative species' litter would decompose relatively faster in stands dominated by conservative species (Hypothesis 2a). Second, any species would decompose faster in stands halfway between ‘conservative’ and ‘acquisitive’ functional composition with a steeper humpback in acquisitive species' litter than in intermediate species' litter, and then in conservative species' litter, as a consequence of high functional diversity (Hypothesis 2b). We tested our hypotheses through a litter decomposition study in a tree diversity experiment in subtropical China. We quantified the leaf litter mass losses for acquisitive, intermediate and conservative species and measured microclimates across 30 stands that represent a range of tree functional diversity and composition over five decomposition periods over 394 days. Increasing stand species richness and stand functional diversity were significantly associated with higher leaf litter decomposition rates across all three functionally contrasting litter species. This positive effect did not change with the litter species' resource acquisition strategies, in partial support of our Hypothesis 1. Increasing stand functional composition along an axis from resource conservative to acquisitive had rather similar humpback relations with leaf litter decomposition rates for all three litter species, which partly supported our Hypothesis 2b but rejected our Hypothesis 2a. Our study provides mechanistic insights into the potential direct and indirect roles of functional trait diversity and composition in driving litter decomposition, and these insights are relevant to many ecosystem types globally.

Abstract

林分功能多样性(RaoQ)与功能组成(CWM trait)对凋落物分解及养分循环等生态系统功能与过程至关重要。由于凋落物质量差异(即资源经济性状种间差异所导致的不同功能策略的凋落物质量差异)与林分微环境差异，林分功能多样性与功能组成会显著改变凋落物分解速率。然而，林分功能多样性与功能组成如何改变不同功能策略物种凋落物分解仍不清楚。 本文提出如下假说:林分功能多样性会促进资源获取型、中间型和保守型物种的凋落物分解速率，但这种促进作用对资源获取型物种最强，对资源保守型物种最弱(假说1)。林分功能组成的影响有两种情况。第一，资源获取型物种凋落物在由资源获取型物种主导的林分中分解速率更快，而资源保守型物种凋落物在由资源保守型物种主导的林分中分解速率更快(假说2a)。第二，所有物种凋落物都在介于保守型与获取型的林分功能组成之间的时候分解最快，这种格局是高功能多样性所导致的(假说2b)。 本文利用中国亚热带树木多样性控制实验检验了以上假说。 结果显示，林分物种多样性与功能多样性会显著促进所有功能策略物种的凋落物分解速率，且这种促进作用在不同功能策略物种间不存在显著差异。这些结果部分支持假说1。林分功能组成与所有功能策略凋落物分解速率呈现“驼峰”关系，这一结果部分支持假说2b。 本文为林分功能多样性与功能组成直接或间接驱动凋落物的分解过程提供机理性见解。
